title: Along the cochlea, place marks pitch
summary: Hair cells near the wide end of the cochlea detect higher pitches, and hair cells nearer the center detect lower pitches.
body: NIDCD calls the cochlea a snail-shaped, fluid-filled structure. A traveling wave along the basilar membrane moves hair cells that sit on it. Hair cells near the wide end detect higher-pitched sounds, such as an infant crying. Hair cells closer to the center detect lower-pitched sounds, such as a large dog barking. The examples are the page's, updated in 2022, not a hearing test.

sources.title: How Do We Hear?
sources.author: NIDCD
sources.note: Supports place along the cochlea: wide-end hair cells for higher pitch, central hair cells for lower pitch.
